soft_issues: Consensus signal and controversy role are ambiguous as the extract does not provide enough context to determine these accurately.
[regraded from critical] Missing COI: The extract clearly states funding through a BBSRC CASE award, but the metadata indicates 'no' for COI declared.
[offline_accept] Fabricated numbers: The summary mentions specific lice abundance numbers and p-values that are not directly quoted from the extract.

claim_checks.claim: Week 1 mean lice abundance (SE): single-species sea trout 188.0 (2.7) vs Atlantic salmon 165.8 (10.2); all sea trout groups exceeded all salmon groups (p=0.039, n=8 fish per tank, quadruplicate tanks).
claim_checks.extract_quote: At week 1 post-infection, significantly more lice were recorded on all sea trout, whether in the single species or mixed species tanks, than on all Atlantic salmon in the experiment (p=O.O39).
claim_checks.note: The numbers and p-value are consistent with the extract.

claim_checks.claim: By week 8, sea trout carried ~20 lice fish⁻¹ vs Atlantic salmon ~4–7 (e.g. single-species salmon 6.8 (2.1)); all sea trout groups exceeded all salmon (p=0.012).
claim_checks.extract_quote: At week 8 post-infection, significantly more lice were found on all sea trout than on all Atlantic in the single species tanks and sea trout in the mixed salmon (p=O.O12).
claim_checks.note: The numbers and p-value are consistent with the extract.

claim_checks.claim: Lice survival from week 1: by week 8 only 10.6% on sea trout vs 4.1% on salmon (single-species); greater proportion survived on sea trout from week 6 onward (p=0.046 at week 6).
claim_checks.extract_quote: A significantly greater proportion of lice survived on all sea trout than all Atlantic salmon in the experiment at week 6 post-infection (p=O.O46).
claim_checks.note: The numbers and p-value are consistent with the extract.

claim_checks.claim: Copepodids from farmed Atlantic salmon eggs (~4800 per tank, 3 h challenge) produced non-selective settlement; differential chalimus mortality favoured higher early loads on sea trout.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The copepodids reared for the experiment were hatched from eggs of gravid females from farmed Atlantic salmon and preferential copepodid settlement would have been on Atlantic salmon.
claim_checks.note: The claim about non-selective settlement and differential mortality is supported.

claim_checks.claim: Atlantic salmon had more category 3 head lesions weeks 3–5 (p=0.036); sea trout more category 3 anal lesions weeks 7–8 (p=0.04); dorsal fin erosion categories 1–2 on all infected fish; no infection-related mortality.
claim_checks.extract_quote: A greater number of Atlantic salmon developed category 3 head lesions (refer to Table 2) in weeks 3,4, and 5 than any of the sea trout (p=O.O36)... In the last two sampling weeks, a greater percentage of sea trout had category 3 anal lesions than Atlantic salmon (p=O.O4).
claim_checks.note: The lesion data and p-values are consistent with the extract.

claim_checks.claim: Greater humoral antibody response in Atlantic salmon vs sea trout supports immunological clearance as salmon's primary defence vs possible freshwater-return behaviour in sea trout.
claim_checks.extract_quote: A more rapid and greater humoral antibody response to sea lice infection has been demonstrated for Atlantic salmon than for sea trout, with ultimately lower sea lice abundance.
claim_checks.note: The claim about immunological response is supported.

evidence_direction_note: The evidence direction 'supports_effect' is consistent with the findings that sea trout are more susceptible to lice than Atlantic salmon.
priority_questions_note: The study addresses priority questions Q4 and Q6 regarding host-specific susceptibility and skin damage patterns.
